aiAgentFacts.fact: Among 646 analysed responses from bereaved dog owners, 536 dogs (83.0%) were euthanased rather than dying unassisted.
Mean age at death was 13.0 years (SD 3.0), pooled across all body sizes — canine life expectancy varies substantially with size, so this describes the cohort, not any individual dog.
The most common reason given for euthanasia was pain and/or suffering (260/536, 48.5%), followed by poor quality of life (133/536, 24.8%).
The reason-for-euthanasia survey item had only FAIR inter-rater reliability (kappa 0.3, 95% CI 0.08-0.52) in validation — the headline 48.5% figure rests on the weakest item in the instrument.
Owner-perceived causes of death were cancer (192/646, 29.7%), 'old age' (190/646, 29.4%) and organ system diseases (144/646, 22.3%).
Of dogs that were euthanased, 411 (76.7%) were euthanased in a veterinary clinic and 122 (22.8%) at the owner's home.
Ninety-five of 646 dogs (14.7%) died without any veterinary involvement.
The survey response rate was 85.7% (655 of 793 invited), unusually high for a bereavement survey; nonetheless owners for whom the loss was too painful to revisit are absent by construction.

historyQuestions: Not prescribed by this paper. Its finding that pain, suffering and quality of life dominate owner decisions supports asking about those domains explicitly and longitudinally, well before a crisis.
redFlags: Not addressed — this study describes deaths retrospectively and defines no clinical thresholds or warning signs.
differentialDiagnosesMentioned: Owner-perceived categories only (cancer, 'old age', organ system diseases); no clinical differential diagnosis is evaluated and no cause was verified post-mortem.
recommendedDiagnosticWorkups: Not addressed — no diagnostic workup is evaluated. The study assesses a survey instrument's findings, not clinical assessment.

limitations: All principal variables are owner-perceived; no cause of death was verified post-mortem

Instrument reliability varies sharply by item — substantial for cause of death (kappa 0.73), moderate for perimortem quality of life (0.49), only fair for reason for euthanasia (0.3, CI approaching zero)
'Old age' accounted for 29.4% of owner-perceived causes and is a description of an ending rather than a mechanism
Volunteer cohort of engaged owners who then chose to complete a bereavement survey; non-responders are unmeasurable and the direction of bias is unknown
Mean age at death pools all body sizes despite large size-related differences in canine life expectancy
Purely descriptive: no approach to end-of-life care is evaluated for its effect on animal or owner outcomes
Deaths occurred largely during the COVID-19 pandemic period (December 2019 to March 2021), which may have affected veterinary access and the setting of euthanasia
